exclusions.query: Nonuniqueness for every finite-mass finite-energy entropy datum
exclusions.reason: The main theorem is existential and uses a specific concentrating datum, so it does not assert generic nonuniqueness.

evidence.quote: For fixed $N,b,T,\lambda$, the colored equations have a unique nonnegative local mild solution with bounded total $H$-norm.

exclusions.query: Failure of uniqueness for fixed finite colored cutoff approximations
exclusions.reason: The fixed finite approximation has a unique local mild solution in the bounded weighted-norm class; the nonuniqueness conclusion concerns the limiting problem.

evidence.quote: Our datum instead has unbounded amplitudes at shrinking spatial scales.
The small relative entropy used in its construction therefore does not place it in these uniqueness classes.

exclusions.query: Contradiction of uniqueness for bounded Maxwellian or small regular perturbations
exclusions.reason: The constructed datum has unbounded amplitudes at shrinking spatial scales and is explicitly distinguished from the cited uniqueness classes.

evidence.quote: A single normalized gain need not become small as the outgoing velocity approaches the axis.
This is the reason for using two successive gains in the axial argument that follows.

exclusions.query: A single near-axis normalized gain must vanish
exclusions.reason: The sharp axial example has a positive limiting normalized gain, so the axial nonconcentration argument requires successive gains.

evidence.quote: This proves [sep:diagonal] without a convergence rate uniform in $T_k$.

exclusions.query: A numerical convergence rate or executable nonuniqueness certificate
exclusions.reason: The separation diagonal explicitly lacks a convergence rate uniform in the shrinking horizon.

outputs.exact_statement: There exist $R<\infty$ and a nonnegative datum $F_0$ with $$\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}_vF_0\subset B_R(0),\qquad \int_\Omega F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\,\mathrm dx\,\mathrm dv<\infty,$$ for which [eq:collision] has two global entropy solutions with local conservation in the sense of Definition 1, differing on a set of positive $(t,x,v)$-measure. Both solutions belong to $C([0,\infty);L^1(\Omega))$. Moreover, for every finite $T$ and every $k\ge0$, they satisfy $$\label{eq:strong-collision-integrability} \int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega \langle v\rangle^k\bigl[Q^+(F,F)+Q^-(F,F)\bigr] \,\mathrm dx\,\mathrm dv\,\mathrm dt<\infty, \qquad \langle v\rangle=(1+|v|^2)^{1/2}.$$

There is a numerical constant $c>0$ such that $$|\bar n|\ge\frac{c}{1+|n|}\qquad
             (n\in\Lambda\setminus\{0\}).
 \label{con:diophantine}$$

The density $F_0$ is nonnegative, has bounded velocity support, and satisfies $$\int F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\,\mathrm dx\,\mathrm dv<\infty.$$ Its truncations with $j\le N$, with or without a seed [con:seed], converge to $F_0$ in weighted $L^1$ for every fixed polynomial velocity weight and in relative entropy with respect to either $M$ or $\mu$. The convergence is uniform for $0

For fixed $N,b,T,\lambda$, the colored equations have a unique nonnegative local mild solution with bounded total $H$-norm. It continues while that norm remains bounded, with the prescribed transfers at retirement times, and depends continuously in this norm on its initial data on every common bounded interval of existence. The norm of each component is continuous between transfers.*


*On every such interval, total mass, momentum, and energy are conserved. The exact local collision-invariant balances hold, with all polynomial velocity fluxes integrable. For $\rho=M$ or $\rho=\mu$, one has at every time of existence $$\mathcal H_\rho(F(t))+
       \int_0^t\mathcal D^b(F(s))\,\mathrm ds
       \le\mathcal H_\rho(F(0)),
 \label{con:finite-entropy}$$ where $\mathcal D^b$ is the entropy dissipation with the same cutoff.

For sufficiently small $s_0$, the sets $\mathcal O_i(t)$ for active labels are pairwise disjoint in the periodic lift. More precisely, $\mathcal O_i(t)\cap\mathcal O_{i'}(t)=\varnothing$ for distinct labels whenever $t\le\min\{L_{s_i},L_{s_{i'}}\}$. Also $$\widehat E_j^\sigma\subset\{s_j<|y|<e^\eta s_j\}.$$

There is a fixed constant $C_*$ such that, with $$\epsilon_s=C_*L_sd_s/s,\qquad \mathcal U_i=f_i+\epsilon_s m_i,$$ and sufficiently small $s_0$, every finite colored evolution obeys $$0\le c_i(t,x,v)\le\mathcal U_i(t,x,v)\qquad (0\le t\le L_{s_i}) \label{cold:upper}$$ as long as that color is active and the solution exists. If, on an interval beginning at $t_1$, one also has $\nu_F^b\ge\kappa>0$, then $$c_i(t,x,v)\le e^{-\kappa(t-t_1)}\mathcal U_i(t,x,v)\qquad (t_1\le t\le L_{s_i}) \label{cold:decay}$$ throughout that interval. None of the constants in [cold:upper] uses a bound on the bath or hot density.

At a fixed $(t,x)$, the velocity measure $f_i(t,x,p)\,\mathrm dp$ is the pushforward of $$\frac{K S(\gamma(z_c-tp_3)/s)}
          {s+t\alpha\gamma S(\gamma(z_c-tp_3)/s)}\,J(w)\,\mathrm dw,\qquad
 \bar p=d_s\bar w,\quad
 p_3=a_s^\sigma(z_c-tp_3)+d_sw_3,
 \label{cold:core-formula}$$ with the initial spatial masks evaluated at $x-tp$. For $t\le L_s$, it is dominated by probability sheets with total amplitude $C/(t+s)$. The remainder $\epsilon_s m_i\,\mathrm dp$ has sheet amplitude at most $$C L_sd_s/s^2\le Cs^{15/2}\le C/(t+s).
 \label{cold:remainder-amplitude}$$ Thus the full upper bound $\mathcal U_i\,\mathrm dp$ has sheet amplitude $C/(t+s)$. In particular, for every fixed $k\ge0$, a main color satisfies $$\int\langle p\rangle^k c_i(t,x,p)\,\mathrm dp\le\frac{C_k}{t+s},\qquad
 \int_{|p|>R}\langle p\rangle^k c_i(t,x,p)\,\mathrm dp
       \le\frac{C_k e^{-c_kR^2}}{t+s}\quad(R\ge3).
 \label{cold:moments}$$

There is a function $\theta_0(s_0)\to0$ as $s_0\downarrow0$ such that, uniformly at all times of existence, $$\sum_{\substack{i\ \mathrm{active}\\x\notin\mathcal O_i(t)}}
       \mathcal U_i(t,x,v)
       \le\theta_0(s_0)e^{-4|v|^2}.
 \label{cold:nonmain-bound}$$ For $0<t\le1$, and any fixed $A,B>0$, the coefficient can instead be taken to be $C_{A,B}t^A s_0^B$. Both assertions remain valid for an arbitrary subset of the active labels.

For some fixed constants $C,C'>0$, $$\left\|\sum_{i:\,s_i=s}\mathcal U_i(L_s)\right\|_H
       \le C s^{-C'}.
 \label{cold:retirement-bound}$$ Moreover, uniformly over the active label sets and all times, $$|\mathcal O(t)|\le\sum_{j\ge1}C s_j^2(1+L_{s_j})
                    \le C s_0^{3/2}.
 \label{cold:tube-volume}$$

For sufficiently small $s_0$ depending on $\delta$, every finite evolution satisfies $$\label{early:source}
 P(c+u,H)\le\frac{C}{t+s_N}H,
 \qquad
 0\le\mathcal S\le C_{A,\delta}t^{A-1}H,
 \qquad 0<t\le t_1,$$ on its interval of existence, for every fixed $A>0$. Here $C$ is independent of $\delta$ and $R_\mu$, and the constants are uniform for all sufficiently small $s_0$. No bound on $h$ is assumed.

Fix $0<t_b<t_1$. There is a function $E_{t_b}(s_0)$ tending to zero as $s_0\to0$ such that, for every finite evolution and every terminal time $t\in[t_b,t_1]$ in its interval of existence, $$\label{early:source-integral}
 \left\|\int_{t_b}^t
    \mathcal S(s,x-(t-s)v,v)\,\mathrm ds\right\|_H

 D_th_{r_N}\le2P(A_N,h_{r_N})+\varepsilon_NH.$$ The bounds and comparison hold on full-measure endpoint sets at each time section, with representatives given by their path formulas.
